_comment: Why this file exists. stop_reason is a published enumeration under Rule 6 — it
appears on every TaskRecord and every `turn` audit record, and a consumer
switches on it. It was pinned only by a hand-kept list inside docs.test.ts,
which checked one direction: a value documented in CONTRACTS.md but never
emitted by the code would have passed, and so would a value the code emits
that nobody documented. Both are drift.
This fixture is the third point that makes the check two-way. The test asserts
the union in prompt_loop.ts, the table in docs/CONTRACTS.md, and the keys here
are the SAME SET — so adding a value means touching all three deliberately,
`truncated` was added 2026-09-05, found by benchmarks/degradation-contract: a
reply the backend cut off twice was allowed to stand and recorded as

stop_reason.answered: the model stopped calling tools of its own accord
stop_reason.empty: the model returned neither text nor a tool call
stop_reason.stall: the same call repeated until the stall limit
stop_reason.truncated: the backend cut the reply off at its token limit, and the one bounded continuation request did not finish it either
stop_reason.apparatus: the run never reached the model — the surface itself could not be used

not_a_bucket: stop_reason is a separate axis from the outcome bucket. The bucket says WHAT happened; this says why the loop stopped. Nothing here maps to result/refusal/apparatus_failure, and a reader combining them is producing a composite verdict this project refuses to publish.
